passwords.note: Its childish, repetitive sound makes it a silly word people type on instinct, which is why it shows up so often.
Its casual "you know it" phrasing plus a tacked-on year feels personal, which is exactly why it never made a leaked list.
Real English words like "contortionist" get picked as passwords for their sound and spelling, so plenty of people land on this same one.
Pairing a beloved character with a year tacks a personal date onto a familiar name, which keeps it out of the most-used tier.
Pallmall is a cigarette brand name, and a single word like that gets picked by people who never bother to make anything up.
